StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:137-140) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterEnergyReset.rationale: Correct slot and correct order, both of which needed checking. C# fires Hook.AfterEnergyReset at CombatManager.cs:650, immediately after ResetEnergy/AddMaxEnergyToCurrent at :644/:648 and BEFORE Hook.BeforeHandDraw (:652) and ModifyHandDraw (:654); the sim fires on_energy_reset at player.py:377, immediately after the same reset (player.py:371-376) and before on_player_turn_start (:378) and modify_hand_draw (:381). The energy therefore lands before any card is playable on both sides. Amount and effect match: PlayerCmd.GainEnergy(base.Amount) then PowerCmd.Remove(this) (EnergyNextTurnPower.cs:22-23) vs EnergyCmd.gain then _expire (powers.py:3449-3450), in the same order. Counter stacking means two Relaxes give one +4 grant on both sides.

guards.rationale: powers.py:3446-3447 player is not self.owner -> return. Identical.

cmds.py:1848-1854 runs hooks.modify_energy_gain and then adds to player.energy, which is C#'s Hook.ModifyEnergyGain + AddEnergy shape. No ported listener on modify_energy_gain distinguishes this source. Third-file citation, not hashed here.

The sim's _expire (powers.py:189-195) pops the power and unregisters it; C#'s PowerCmd.Remove (PowerCmd.cs:287-295) additionally fires power.AfterRemoved, which this power does not implement, so the two are observationally identical. Same treatment as the _expire entries in audit/records/power/duplication.json and audit/records/power/flame_barrier.json, per binding rule 3.

The ported card Relax (cards/relax.py:43-47) and the ported Trash Heap card Outmaneuver (cards/trash_heap_cards.py:220-241), both with applier=ctx.player. C#'s Relax.cs / Outmaneuver.cs pass an applier too, and unlike most of this batch the sim's callers DO pass applier=, so the recurring missing-applier shape does not apply here.
